cells.tense: Right now you're at the bench, deciding what gets built next and meaning it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're building and finish the next small piece today, then stop and let it stand.
cells.core:
You say 'this, not that' and then your hands follow the sentence. Deciding and doing sit in the same place, which is why what you make holds up and other people can lean on it. You tend the thing as it takes shape without forcing it, and you can tell a step that's ready from one that's still raw.

There's nothing here to repair. The next thing this steadiness is free to feed is showing the method: let one other person watch you make the next move, and see whether the direction gets clearer or heavier with a witness in the room. If it gets heavier, that's worth knowing too, and nothing about today rides on the result.
cells.sheetLine: You're building on purpose, and it's holding.
cells.verb: building something new with skill, raising a structure that didn't exist before
cells.place: the part of life where direction gets chosen and held

cells.tense: You're three moves ahead, bracing for a structure that isn't built yet and might not be yours to build.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're trying to force into place and leave it alone for one day, then look at what still needs building.
cells.core:
You build from what you actually see, and what you make fits the ground it's on. Right now you're pushing ahead of the materials. You're laying plans for a version that hasn't arrived, and the pushing has become the work, so the building has slowed or stopped without anyone deciding that.

The cost is that you're carrying a future nobody asked you to carry, and the people around you feel the pressure more than they feel a direction. What Passage does is what's needed here — cross toward what connects instead of what controls. One day of not forcing, so you can hear what the thing actually needs rather than what you've decided it should become.

cells.tense: You're still standing in a doorway you already walked through, blueprint folded in your pocket.
cells.ask: Write down the one next step you'd take if you were going to build this, and read it out loud once.
cells.core:
You know what you're making and you move toward it, and other people can feel that things make sense when you're in the room. These days the direction has gone quiet. You're not building, and you may not be letting yourself want to, which keeps the blueprint folded where nobody can question it, including you.

Effort isn't the shortage; what's in short supply is the clarity that comes from standing inside your own authority. The way back is what Command does — charge that authority directly. Name the next step out loud, alone, and let it be real in the air before anyone else hears it. If it sounds wrong when you say it, that's a useful answer, not a failure.

cells.tense: The pen is down on the table, but you're still writing the plan in how you spend your days.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're already steering and call it a choice you made, in your own words, once.
cells.core:
You build from genuine engagement, and what you make carries your direction because you felt your way into it first. Right now the building is happening, but you describe it as just how things go. A direction is being held without anyone saying so, and the person who gets the least credit for it is the one who set it.

The way back is to go simpler, the way Resolve does: reduce the story to the feeling that started it. Say out loud that you picked this, once, in words you'd actually use. Momentum gathers from there, not from a better explanation.
